title: Greensboro police pass out hydration packs amid heat wave - NewsBreak
text:
By Justin Lundy ,
1 hours ago
GREENSBORO, N.C. (WGHP) — As the temperatures intensify, so does the risk for those who have no way to escape it.
Greensboro police are taking extra steps to check on some of the most vulnerable by making sure they have access to water, shade and other resources they need to stay safe.
What the officers are carrying may look like goody bags, but they could actually save someone’s life.
Beat the Heat hydration packs are what Captain K.B Johnson and other Greensboro officers are handing out to those in need.
It was started by Sergeant Shawn Patterson. He saw a need for it last year during the hottest days. He bought some hydration essentials, and his squad passed them out.
On a scorching Wednesday afternoon, officers made pit stops along Summitt Avenue in east Greensboro.
“We saw people who were … making their way through some of the neighborhoods in District Four where people don’t have vehicles and have got to walk an extended distance to get to work, to get to the grocery stores,” Johnson said.
Johnson advised everyone to look out for their neighbors during stretches of extreme heat and for themselves.
“Monitor yourself. If you’re hot, take a break. It’s not worth getting to the store 10 minutes faster, especially if you’ve got medical issues or you’re elderly. You may need to slow down a little bit. We all need to slow down in this type of weather,” Johnson said.
Johnson says you can drop off donations for the hydration packs at the police headquarters at 100 E. Police Plaza in Greensboro.
They’re taking donations of any of the following:
bottled water Gatorade or other bottled electrolyte drinks electrolyte packets (to package with bottled water) granola bars Copyright 2026 Nexstar Media, Inc. All rights reserved.
